system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Universal solution
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Definition via homomorphisms into all solutions, and universal models in the chase literature. Covers the chase as the way to compute it, naive evaluation of UCQs for certain answers, and non-existence cases (a failing chase branch, no universal solution despite solutions existing).

ATOMS:
- CS-DB-C05-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: For a data-exchange setting $\sigma=(S,T,\Sigma_{st},\Sigma_t)$ and a source instance $I$, a universal solution is a universal model of $I$ and $\Sigma_{st}\cup\Sigma_t$ restricted to the target schema $T$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0039-s22] Where the universal solution for a data-exchange setting σ = (S, T, Σst, Σt) and the instance I is a universal model for I and Σst ∪Σt restricted to schema T.
- CS-DB-C05-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: A universal solution for a source instance I has a homomorphism into every other solution for I.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0054-s17] A universal solution has a homomorphism into any other solution for I.
- CS-DB-C05-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: A finite instance $U$ is a (strong) universal model of $I$ and $\Sigma$ if $U$ is a model of $I$ and $\Sigma$ and $U$ has a homomorphism into every finite and every infinite model of $I$ and $\Sigma$. A weak universal model is required to map homomorphically only into the finite models.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0037-s25] ▶Deﬁnition 65. [16] A ﬁnite instance U is said to be a weak universal model of I and Σ if U is a model of I and Σ, and if for any ﬁnite model J of I and Σ, it is that U →J.
    [CS-DB-p0037-s26] If U →J.
    [CS-DB-p0037-s27] Also for all inﬁnite models J of I and Σ, then U is said to be a strong universal model or simply a universal model.
- CS-DB-C05-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a set of tgds and egds, a universal model of $I$ and $\Sigma$ exists if and only if the core chase terminates and does not fail on $I$ and $\Sigma$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0038-s22] ▶Theorem 70. [16] Let I be an instance and Σ a set of tgds and egds.
    [CS-DB-p0038-s23] Then there exists a universal model of I and Σ iﬀthe core-chase algorithm terminates and does not fail on input I and Σ.
- CS-DB-C05-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: If a universal solution $J$ exists for a null-free source instance $I$ and a data-exchange setting $\sigma$, then for every union of conjunctive queries $Q$ the certain answers equal the naïve evaluation of $Q$ on $J$, i.e. $cert_\sigma(Q,I)=Q_{na\ddot{i}ve}(J)$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0040-s11] ▶Theorem 75. [19] Let σ = (S, T, Σst, Σt) be a data-exchange setting and I an instance over the source instance that does not contain nulls such that there exists a universal solution J for I and σ.
    [CS-DB-p0040-s12] Then, certσ(Q, I) = Qnaïve(J) for any Q ∈UCQ.
- CS-DB-C05-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: For an instance $I$ and a set $\Sigma$ of tgds and egds, any finite instance returned by the standard chase (when it does not fail) is a universal model of $I$ and $\Sigma$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0038-s03] Then any ﬁnite instance returned by the standard-chase algorithm is a universal model of I and Σ.
- CS-DB-C05-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: If the standard chase on a source instance $I$ and $\Sigma_{st}\cup\Sigma_t$ has a failing branch, then no universal solution exists for $I$ under the data-exchange setting.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0039-s30] ▶Theorem 73. [19] Let σ = (S, T, Σst, Σt) be a data-exchange setting and I a source instance such that there is a failing branch for the standard chase with input I and Σst ∪Σt.
    [CS-DB-p0039-s31] Then there is no universal solution for I and σ.
- CS-DB-C05-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: It is undecidable whether a universal solution exists for a given data-exchange setting and a given source instance.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0039-s25] In particular, it means that the universal solution can be computed by the chase algorithms and that it is undecidable if the universal solution exists for a given data-exchange setting and a given source instance.
- CS-DB-C05-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: A data-exchange setting can have a solution but no universal solution. For example, with $\Sigma_{st}=\{S(x,y)\to R(x,y)\}$, $\Sigma_t=\{R(x,y)\to\exists z\,R(y,z)\}$ and $I=\{S(a,b)\}$, there is no universal solution, yet $J=\{R(a,b),R(b,b)\}$ is a solution.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0040-s04] σ = ({S}, {R}, {S(x, y) →R(x, y)}, {R(x, y) →∃z R(y, z)})
    [CS-DB-p0040-s05] and the source instance I = {S(a, b)}.
    [CS-DB-p0040-s06] Clearly there is no universal solution for this setting, but there exists solution J = {R(a, b), R(b, b)}.
